hop_1_perplexity.topic: On-Chain Metrics Integration for Crypto Signal Scoring
hop_1_perplexity.context: I run a multi-source crypto signal pipeline (Striker engine, 140K signals in DuckDB) on Coinbase Advanced Trade. I've identified CryptoQuant (5 endpoints: exchange-reserve, exchange-netflow-total, exchange-inflow-total, stablecoin USDT/USDC netflow, stablecoin reserve) and Whale Alert (3000+ queued messages) as highest-signal-density unwired sources. Current scoring: edge_score = source_prior × confidence × relevance × novelty × recency × cross_source_boost × fp_penalty × tier_mult × bluechip_mult. Need to understand: lead-lag relationships between exchange reserves/netflows and BTC/ETH price action, stablecoin flow interpretation (is inflow to exchanges buying pressure or selling?), how to weight on-chain vs momentum vs sentiment in multi-signal fusion, documented threshold values with predictive power, API reliability patterns for CryptoQuant/Whale Alert, and how professional quant systems weight these metrics. API base: api.cryptoquant.com/v1/ with access token auth.

hop_2_perplexity.topic: DuckDB Tiered Retention & Time-Series Scaling for Signal Data
hop_2_perplexity.context: My signal pipeline stores ~140K crypto signal_scores in DuckDB (~8K/hour from Striker). Sources queue data from 80+ Telegram channels, Whale Alert (3K unprocessed), and on-chain metrics. Current issues: no partitioning, no tiered retention, single writer (no concurrency safety), 31 unprocessed Telegram exports piling up. Need to research: DuckDB time-series partitioning (daily granularity with date pruning — native or UNION ALL views?), Parquet cold storage patterns (ZSTD vs Snappy for variable-width signal data), concurrent writer safety with flock, retention policies for ageing out signal data (delete vs move vs mark stale), and schema migration strategies when adding new signal sources without downtime. Also how quant systems handle 100K+ row insertions/hour on a budget server (2GB RAM target).

hop_3_perplexity.topic: Boot Persistence & Self-Healing for Multi-Agent Auto-Trading Stacks
hop_3_perplexity.context: I run a swarm of autonomous LLM agents (5 Hermes/OpenClaw profiles) with a live crypto trading backend (Freqtrade + Coinbase, $10 real wallet, 3 pairs) and signal pipeline (Striker, 140K signals). Everything runs via systemd user units and cron. The biggest unresolved risk is boot persistence: if the server restarts or an agent process crashes, there's no verified auto-resurrection. Current issues: Nemoclaw gateway DOWN, 2 Freqtrade instances running same config (kill one), Striker health stale since Jun 8, OpenRouter budget exceeded ($211/day vs $30 threshold). Need to research: production watchdog patterns for agent resurrection, systemd timer vs cron tradeoffs for agent-adjacent jobs, fencing patterns to prevent duplicate Freqtrade instances, exponential backoff retry wrappers for idempotent pipeline jobs, and how to distinguish 'processing long request' from 'crashed' for LLM agents.
